## How to read this lecture

This is a **live run**, not theory: every stage executes package code and shows the
numbers for a real locus — FRI, `Chr4:269745 G>A` (stop_gained), 1001 Genomes.

The order of stages follows the LGC/KBioscience KASP guide (+ EasyKASP 2025).

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidymarkers); library(here); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
})
```

::: {.notes}
Source: `dev/lecture/kasp-slides.qmd`; render with `sh dev/lecture/render.sh`
(puts OligoArrayAux on PATH). Each slide is one stage; its notes say what to say.
:::

## Stage 0. What KASP is and what the design really decides

- Two **allele-specific** primers (AS1/AS2) carrying different fluorophores, plus one **common** primer (COM).
- Specificity rests on **one** base at the 3' end of the AS primer.
- So everything is decided by: target choice → 3' window → thermodynamics → genome specificity.

::: {.notes}
One slide, one idea. From here we walk the stages of the guide and show, at each
one, what was checked and what was found.
:::

## Stage 1. The target: a meaningful variant with a clean 3' window

```{r}
#| label: data
genome   <- ath_genome()                                   # TAIR10, cached in marker_cache_dir()
gene     <- ensembl_gene("AT4G00650")                      # FRI
variants <- ensembl_variants(gene$chrom, gene$start, gene$end)
snp      <- pick_target_snp(variants, genome, gene)
snp |> dplyr::select(id, chrom, pos, ref, alt, consequence, n_3p, seed_hits)
```

**What is checked:** consequence severity (VEP `impact` or canonical SO terms),
the absence of *other* variants in the 3' window (`n_3p`), and uniqueness of the
3' seed (`seed_hits`). Complementary pairs (A/T, C/G) are skipped — a 3' base
cannot tell them apart.

::: {.notes}
Here `n_3p = 0` — no other 1001 Genomes variant sits in the target's 3' window.
`seed_hits` is the better of the two strands; the discrepancy with the
specificity stage is covered in stage 7.
:::

## Stage 2. Design window and flanks (a hint, not a decision)

```{r}
#| label: window
win_len <- length(genome_seq(genome, "Chr4", snp$pos - 150L, snp$pos + 150L))
glue::glue("{win_len} nt design window (Chr4 {snp$pos - 150}..{snp$pos + 150})") |> as.character()
strand_gc_hint(genome, snp$chrom, snp$pos)
```

EasyKASP suggests placing the AS primer where the flank GC gives a workable Tm —
but strand and length are still decided here by physics (`DECIPHER`), not by an
eyeball rule.

::: {.notes}
`strand_gc_hint()` is only a hint about where to look; the algorithm picks the final strand.
:::

## Stage 3. The AS primer: the search and the Tm/GC windows

How the primer is "moved": enumerate **both strands × length 20–27 × position and
base of the stabilising mismatch**, then keep those that land in the Tm/GC windows.

```{r}
#| label: design
assay <- assemble_kasp_assay(genome, snp, variants = variants, flank = 150L,
                             strands = c("+", "-"), tm_range = c(58, 64), clean_3p = 5L)

raw <- design_as_primers(assay$template$seq, assay$template$snp_i,
                         snp$ref, snp$alt, strands = c("+", "-"))
tibble::tibble(
  placements     = nrow(raw),
  Tm_range       = glue::glue("{round(min(raw$tm),1)}-{round(max(raw$tm),1)} C"),
  pass_Tm_window = sum(dplyr::between(raw$tm, 58, 64)),
  pass_GC_window = sum(dplyr::between(raw$gc, 0.35, 0.70))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.notes}
112 placements; the Tm window [58,64] cuts more than half of them (47.7–66 C).
It is the length/strand search that moves Tm into the window. Change tm_range to
see it shift.
:::

## Stage 3 (continued). What the algorithm chose, and why not the loudest

```{r}
#| label: as-choice
ranked <- assay$as_candidates |>
  dplyr::arrange(n_3p, n_var, dplyr::desc(discrimination), wobble,
                 seed_hits, abs(tm - 60), dg_3p, as_length)
cat("CHOSEN (row 1 of the ranking):\n")
ranked |> dplyr::slice_head(n = 1) |>
  dplyr::select(strand, as_length, tm, gc, discrimination, n_3p, n_var, seed_hits) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
cat("\nHighest discrimination, but rejected:\n")
ranked |> dplyr::slice_max(discrimination, n = 4) |>
  dplyr::select(strand, as_length, tm, gc, discrimination, n_3p, n_var, seed_hits) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

**Finding:** the placements with discrimination **0.97** (minus strand) overlap
**2–3** other 1001 Genomes variants in their footprint; the chosen 27-mer on the
plus strand overlaps only **1** (`n_var`). In this guide, variant load in the
footprint outranks discrimination.

::: {.notes}
This answers "why 0.93 and not 0.97": not because 0.93 is "better", but because
0.97 has extra variants sitting in its footprint. The ranking is lexicographic.
:::

## Stage 4. Discrimination and 3' stability of the chosen AS primer

```{r}
#| label: eff
assay$efficiency |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
    caption = "ref_on/ref_off — AS-ref on its own/other allele; alt_* likewise")
```

Discrimination = (ref_on − ref_off + alt_on − alt_off) / 2, computed by `DECIPHER`
(Taq-aware: hybridisation **and** extension from the 3' end), not by an empirical
formula.

::: {.notes}
`ref_on 1.00`, `ref_off 0.02` — the matching allele extends, the other hardly at all.
:::

## Stage 5. The common primer: Tm ≥ AS and an amplicon ≤ 100 bp

```{r}
#| label: com
assay$assay |>
  dplyr::count(com_tm_ge_as = com_tm >= mean(assay$thermo$tm[assay$thermo$name != "COM"]),
               amplicon_ok = dplyr::between(amplicon, 50, 100)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "5 COM placements: how many close the amplicon and hold Tm")
assay$assay |>
  dplyr::select(rank, strand, com, len, com_tm, n_var, amplicon) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

::: {.notes}
COM is placed on the same strand as AS so that the amplicon closes; the guide
requires COM Tm no lower than AS and a product shorter than 100 bp (EasyKASP).
:::

## Stage 6. Structural QC: hairpins, homo- and heterodimers

```{r}
#| label: struct
assay$thermo |>
  dplyr::select(primer, len, tm, gc, hairpin_dg, terminal_dg) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "OligoArrayAux: hairpin and 3'-end dG37")
pal <- find_palindromes(c(AS_ref = assay$assay$as_ref[1],
                          AS_alt = assay$assay$as_alt[1], COM = assay$assay$com[1]))
data.frame(primer = names(pal), inverted_repeats = vapply(pal, nrow, integer(1)))
```

```{r}
#| label: dimers
ggplot(assay$complementarity, aes(a, b, fill = dg)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(dg, 1)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "firebrick", high = "white", name = "dG37") +
  coord_equal() + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Duplexes: cross- and self-dimers")
```

::: {.notes}
All three primers have a positive hairpin dG (none forms). There are no inverted
repeats. The strongest pair is COM×AS-alt, dG37 ≈ −3.3, against a threshold of −9.
:::

## Stage 7. Genome specificity: off-targets

```{r}
#| label: specific
assay$specificity |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "3' seed (15 nt, ≤1 mismatch) across TAIR10 — how many genomic sites")
```

**Finding:** the AS primer's 3' seed occurs **dozens** of times in the genome at
one mismatch. That is expected for a short seed and does **not** fail the test:
the full primer decides, not the seed. It is checked directly:

```{r}
#| label: pcr
assay$amplicons |> knitr::kable(caption = "virtual PCR: REF yields 1 product, ALT yields 0")
```

::: {.notes}
One nuance: `seed_hits` (stage 1) is the better of the two strands, while AS
landed on the strand where the seed is "louder". The seed scan is therefore a
filter, not a verdict; the verdict comes from in-silico PCR (1/0) and the
full-primer FM scan.
:::

## Stage 7 (continued). FM index: a full-primer scan

```{r}
#| label: fm
fm <- marker_fm_index(genome, basename = fs::path(marker_cache_dir(), "tair10_fm"))
fm_hits <- specificity_fm(c(AS_ref = assay$assay$as_ref[1], AS_alt = assay$assay$as_alt[1],
                            COM = assay$assay$com[1]), fm, nthreads = 2L)
fm_hits |> knitr::kable(caption = "Rsubread FM index: how many genomic loci the full primer matches")
```

The index is built once (cached), the genome is not loaded into memory, and mapping is multithreaded.

::: {.notes}
The full primers are unique (one locus) — that is what closes the off-target question.
:::

## Stage 9. Acceptance and ordering

```{r}
#| label: checks
marker_design_checks(assay) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: order
marker_primer_table(assay, gene) |>
  dplyr::select(role, oligo_id, sequence, tm, gc, length) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.notes}
14 criteria: amplicon length, AS/COM Tm, COM≥AS, GC, homopolymers, SSRs,
inverted repeats, hairpins, dimers, discrimination, in-silico PCR. The FAM/HEX
tails and the IDT/LGC files come from `export_primers()`.
:::

## Stage 10. The guide's full checklist: structure and thermodynamics

Every LGC/KBioscience + EasyKASP 2025 recommendation → the package function that
implements it → our run.

```{r}
#| label: recs-struct
chk <- marker_design_checks(assay)
obs <- function(c) chk$observed[match(c, chk$criterion)]
aa  <- assay$assay[1, ]
wt  <- assay$as_candidates |>
  dplyr::arrange(n_3p, n_var, dplyr::desc(discrimination), wobble, seed_hits, abs(tm - 60), dg_3p, as_length) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)

tibble::tibble(
  Recommendation = c("Short amplicon", "SNP at the terminal 3' base", "AS length",
                     "AS Tm (own allele)", "AS GC", "Strand: GC≈45%, no repeats",
                     "Stabilising mismatch −2/−3", "Last 5 nt free of other SNPs"),
  Threshold = c("50–100 bp", "required", "20–28 nt", "55–65 °C", "40–60%",
                "both strands", "1–3 nt from 3'", "0 variants"),
  `In the package` = c("marker_design_checks()", "make_as_primer()", "design_as_primers()",
                       "primer_tm() (TmCalculator)", "gc_frac()", "strand × lengths × search",
                       "stab_ats (scan)", "n_3p: IRanges::countOverlaps"),
  Run = c(glue::glue("{obs('amplicon length (bp)')} bp"),
             glue::glue("{assay$snp$ref}>{assay$snp$alt}"),
             glue::glue("{wt$as_length} nt"),
             glue::glue("{round(obs('AS Tm (C)'),1)} °C"),
             glue::glue("{round(100*obs('AS GC'),0)}%"),
             glue::glue("{wt$strand} chosen"),
             glue::glue("no mismatch needed"),
             glue::glue("{aa$as_n_3p} variant(s)"))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.notes}
On the left, what the guide recommends; in the middle, the function that does it;
on the right, the result of our run. Every value is live, none invented.
:::

## Stage 10 (continued). Checklist: the common primer and structure

```{r}
#| label: recs-com
obs_c <- function(label) chk$observed[match(label, chk$criterion)]
tibble::tibble(
  Recommendation = c("COM length", "COM GC", "COM Tm ≥ AS Tm", "Homopolymers < 4",
                     "Hairpins (ΔG37)", "Any-pair dimers (ΔG37)", "Inverted repeats",
                     "SSR 2–4 nt"),
  Threshold = c("18–25 nt", "40–60%", "≥ AS Tm", "< 4 nt", "≥ −3", "≥ −9", "none", "none"),
  `In the package` = c("design_common_primers()", "gc_frac()", "com_tm vs AS Tm",
                     "has_run()", "primer_thermo()/OligoArrayAux", "dimer_thermo()/OligoArrayAux",
                     "find_palindromes() (Biostrings)", "find_repeats()"),
  Run = c(glue::glue("{aa$len} nt"),
             glue::glue("{round(100*aa$com_gc,0)}%"),
             glue::glue("{round(chk$observed[match('COM Tm >= AS Tm', chk$criterion)],1)} °C"),
             glue::glue("{chk$observed[match('longest homopolymer (bp)', chk$criterion)]}"),
             glue::glue("{round(chk$observed[match('worst hairpin dG37', chk$criterion)],1)}"),
             glue::glue("{round(chk$observed[match('worst cross-dimer dG37', chk$criterion)],1)}"),
             glue::glue("{chk$observed[match('inverted repeat (arms>=4, loop<=6)', chk$criterion)]}"),
             glue::glue("{chk$observed[match('SSR (2-4 nt, >=3 copies)', chk$criterion)]}"))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.notes}
Call out the AS1–AS2 pair separately: in KASP it is expected to be the strongest,
because the primers are nearly identical and compete for one site. That is
normal, not a defect.
:::

## Stage 10 (continued). Checklist: discrimination, specificity, validation

```{r}
#| label: recs-spec
spec <- assay$specificity
fm_n <- paste(fm_hits$hits, collapse = "/")
tibble::tibble(
  Recommendation = c("Discrimination on–off", "Avoid G:T / C:A wobble",
                     "Specificity: exactly one product", "Pre-screen the 3' seed",
                     "A full-primer off-target is fatal", "Variant annotation", "Validation: controls"),
  `In the package` = c("pcr_efficiency() (DECIPHER, Taq)", "wobble_mismatch()",
                     "in_silico_pcr() (matchProbePair)", "specificity_seed() (PDict)",
                     "specificity_fm() (Rsubread FM index)", "annotate_variants() (TxDb/VEP)",
                     "wet lab (not code)"),
  Run = c(glue::glue("{round(assay$efficiency$ref_on,2)} on / {round(assay$efficiency$ref_off,2)} off"),
             glue::glue("{assay$specificity$seed[1]} — G:T"),
             glue::glue("REF 1 / ALT 0"),
             glue::glue("seed hits: {spec$hits[1]}/{spec$hits[2]}/{spec$hits[3]}"),
             glue::glue("{fm_n} locus/loci for AS-ref/alt/COM"),
             glue::glue("stop_gained (AT4G00650)"),
             glue::glue("REF / ALT / het / NTC"))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.notes}
Two different levels of specificity: the seed (a filter) and the full primer (the
verdict). The AS seed returns dozens of hits at one mismatch — that is normal;
in-silico PCR + FM decide.
:::

## How to present this material

- **On stage:** this deck — `sh dev/lecture/render.sh` →
  `_site/dev/lecture/kasp-slides.html`. The `n` key toggles speaker notes on each
  slide; `s` opens presenter mode.
- **To read:** the `vignette("kasp-intro")` narrative.
- **Live run:** `Rscript inst/scripts/run_kasp.R` (numbers and panels in `results/`).

The deck source is `dev/lecture/kasp-slides.qmd`; the `README.md` next to it has the
commands.

::: {.notes}
Show order: 0→1→…→10, running the chunk at each stage and discussing the number.
Finish on the checklist, as "this is how we hand over acceptance".
:::
